title: Introduction
coreMove: Separate the tasks that require uninterrupted cognition from the tasks that merely keep you visibly occupied.
sourcePressure: The source frame defines deep work and shallow work, then states the deep-work hypothesis without adding unsupported anecdotes.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says fewer distractions are nice; the real point is that different tasks make different demands on cognition and deserve different protection.

counterintuition: productivity is not about doing more
tryThisNow: turn off notifications for five minutes

exampleSpecs.domain: a legal aid attorney preparing a last-minute housing injunction
exampleSpecs.audience: a lawyer deciding which tasks deserve her protected morning
exampleSpecs.stakes: a family may lose an apartment if the argument is thin or late
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she moves case-law synthesis onto the protected morning block and pushes docket-label cleanup to the late-afternoon admin slot
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a printed eviction notice clipped to a yellow legal pad at 7:42 a.m.
mustAvoid: email triage as the whole scene

exampleSpecs.domain: a semiconductor layout engineer reviewing a power grid failure
exampleSpecs.audience: a technical specialist sorting deep analysis from routine updates
exampleSpecs.stakes: a tapeout slips if the failure mode is misread
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he labels the voltage-drop diagnosis as deep work and refuses to mix it with status replies until the waveform is understood
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a thermal plot glowing red across the left side of a workstation monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: a museum registrar reconciling provenance records before a loan
exampleSpecs.audience: a cultural worker whose day mixes precision thinking with clerical churn
exampleSpecs.stakes: a disputed artifact cannot travel unless the record is clean
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she separates the provenance chain reconstruction from label printing and assigns each to a different attention state
exampleSpecs.firstImage: cotton gloves beside three accession folders on a metal cart

exampleSpecs.domain: a trauma nurse educator rewriting a simulation protocol
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainer who keeps confusing preparation with production
exampleSpecs.stakes: new nurses may miss the airway cue if the simulation script stays vague
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a failed practice run, she marks scenario design as deep work and supply restocking as shallow work
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a laminated code sheet lying beside an unused oxygen mask

exampleSpecs.domain: an indie game sound designer building an adaptive audio cue
exampleSpecs.audience: a creative worker tempted to treat all production tasks alike
exampleSpecs.stakes: the game feels flat if the boss-fight cue fails to respond to player state
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she blocks the branching cue logic as deep work and leaves file naming for the end of the day
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six waveform lanes stacked under a flickering boss arena preview

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal grants analyst drafting a climate-resilience application
exampleSpecs.audience: a public-sector analyst deciding what kind of attention the proposal needs
exampleSpecs.stakes: the town loses matching funds if the risk narrative is weak
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes two columns labeled deep and shallow, placing risk-model interpretation in one and attachment uploads in the other
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a flood map spread beside a half-completed grant portal

skillTargets: classify tasks by cognitive demand in unfamiliar jobs
choose which work deserves protected attention first
distinguish shallow usefulness from deep value
apply the deep-work hypothesis without turning it into anti-distraction advice

tryThisNowSpec: Scan the next three tasks on your actual list and mark exactly one as cognitively demanding enough to require an uninterrupted block.
